detail:
Mayo Clinic describes treatment for Chiari malformation as depending on the situation: when the malformation is not causing symptoms, no treatment may be needed, although the condition may still be checked over time with exams and MRIs. When headaches or other types of pain are the primary symptom, Mayo Clinic notes that pain medicine may be used to help ease the pain.

Chiari malformations that cause symptoms are often treated with surgery, Mayo Clinic states, with the goal of preventing further damage; surgery can also ease or stabilize symptoms, lowers pressure on the cerebellum and spinal cord, and restores the usual flow of spinal fluid. The most common operation described is posterior fossa decompression, which removes a small piece of bone at the back of the skull. When too much fluid collects in the brain (hydrocephalus), a tube called a shunt may be placed to drain the extra fluid. Mayo Clinic also notes the risks of surgery, including infection, cerebrospinal fluid leakage, and wound healing problems, and that surgery cannot reverse nerve injury that has already happened.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing Chiari malformation and its treatments.
summary: Mayo Clinic describes Chiari malformation care ranging from monitoring with exams and MRIs when there are no symptoms, to pain medicine, to posterior fossa decompression surgery that relieves pressure and restores spinal fluid flow.
takeaways: no symptoms can mean monitoring rather than treatment, per the source
posterior fossa decompression is the most common surgery described
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Chiari Malformation: from monitoring to decompression surgery
